input: Write a due diligence memo on Databricks

business.claim: Databricks sells a Data + AI Platform built on an open lakehouse architecture that unifies enterprise data, governance, analytics, machine learning and AI applications; it is marketed to organizations and their data/AI teams. (company claim)
The current product suite named by Databricks includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse and Unity Catalog. (company claim)
Databricks says it was founded in 2013 by the original creators of the lakehouse architecture and open-source projects including Apache Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow and Unity Catalog. (company claim)
The company is headquartered in San Francisco, has 30+ offices around the globe, and says it serves customers worldwide. (company claim)
Databricks reported opening or expanding regional presence in London, Singapore, Latin America and the Middle East as part of global expansion. (company claim)

traction.claim: Databricks said more than 20,000 organizations worldwide, including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian and Unilever, rely on its platform; it also said 70% of the Fortune 500 use it. (company claim)
Databricks reported more than 1,000 customers consuming at over $1 million revenue run-rate and more than 100 customers consuming at over $10 million revenue run-rate. (company claim)

Fox Corporation announced a multi-year strategic partnership naming Databricks its platform of choice for data, AI applications and agents; Fox said it uses Lakebase, Genie Code, Unity Gateway and Genie Ontology. (company claim)
Databricks says AXA France unified 200TB of data from 54 sources on its platform to provide personalized services to more than 6.3 million customers. (company customer-story claim)

The 2024 Series J announcement reported 500+ customers consuming at over $1 million annual revenue run-rate and Databricks SQL at a $600 million revenue run-rate, up more than 150% year over year. (company claim)

team.claim: Databricks currently lists Ali Ghodsi as Co-founder and CEO; Ion Stoica as Co-founder and Executive Chair; Matei Zaharia as Co-founder and CTO; Patrick Wendell as Co-founder and VP of Engineering; Reynold Xin as Co-founder and Chief Architect; Andy Konwinski as Co-founder; and Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji as Co-founder and SVP of Field Engineering. (company claim)

The current executive page lists Andy Kofoid as President, Global Field Operations; David Conte as CFO; Amy Reichanadter as Chief People Officer; Trâm Phi as SVP and General Counsel; Ron Gabrisko as CRO; Rick Schultz as CMO; Hatim Shafique as COO; Fermín Serna as Chief Security Officer; Naveen Zutshi as CIO; Vinod Marur as SVP of Engineering; David Meyer as SVP of Products; and Adam Conway as SVP of Products. (company claim)
CFO David Conte previously served as Splunk CFO for eight years and CFO of Opsware before its $1.65 billion acquisition by HP; Databricks appointed him CFO in 2019. (company claim)

Databricks announced in 2016 that Ali Ghodsi became CEO while Ion Stoica became Executive Chairman; the announcement also identified Matei Zaharia as co-founder and CTO and Patrick Wendell as VP of Engineering. (company claim)

funding.claim: In August 2026 Databricks announced it closed a $5 billion strategic funding round at a $190 billion valuation, led by Coatue with Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price and Sixth Street Growth among the named participants. (company claim)

Reuters reported that Databricks raised more than $4 billion in a Series L at a $134 billion valuation in December 2025; the round was led by Insight Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company and J.P. Morgan Asset Management. (Reuters report)

Databricks announced a $10 billion Series J financing at a $62 billion valuation in December 2024, with $8.6 billion completed at announcement; Thrive Capital led and Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, GIC, Insight Partners and WCM Investment Management co-led. (company claim)
Databricks announced a $1.6 billion Series H at a $38 billion post-money valuation in August 2021, led by Counterpoint Global (Morgan Stanley). (company claim)

The latest publicly opened primary source establishes the last known valuation at $190 billion as of August 2026; Databricks remains private in the sources reviewed. (company claim for valuation; private-status observation)

financial_signals.claim: Databricks reported a revenue run-rate above $7 billion, year-over-year growth above 80% in Q2 2026, positive adjusted free cash flow over the last 12 months, Lakehouse revenue run-rate above $1.5 billion with growth above 100% year over year, and Lakebase revenue run-rate above $100 million. (company claim)

Reuters reported Databricks exceeded a $4.8 billion revenue run-rate in Q3 2025, up more than 55% year over year; its AI-products and data-warehousing businesses each exceeded a $1 billion run-rate, and it reported positive free cash flow over the prior 12 months. (Reuters report)

Databricks said in December 2024 that it expected to cross a $3 billion revenue run-rate and reach positive free cash flow in the quarter ending January 31, 2025, and reported non-GAAP subscription gross margins above 80%. (company claim)
Revelio Labs estimated 14,321 worldwide employees as of March 2026, up 2.2% year over year from 2025; it also reported 1,211 active job postings in 2026, down 12.0% from 2025. (aggregator estimate)
Reuters reported that Databricks had about 7,000 employees in December 2024 and that management had slowed headcount expansion and offshored some jobs to lower costs. (Reuters report)

legal_and_regulatory.claim: A federal docket shows Rebecca Makkai and Jason Reynolds filed a copyright complaint against Databricks, Inc. and Mosaic ML, Inc. in the Northern District of California on May 2, 2024. (court record)

Plaintiffs' counsel reports that the consolidated In re Mosaic LLM Litigation alleges unauthorized use of copyrighted books in MosaicML/Databricks model training, that a Second Amended Consolidated Complaint added allegations concerning DBRX, and that on April 21, 2026 the court denied defendants' motion to dismiss and motion to strike DBRX-related allegations. These are litigation allegations and counsel's procedural account, not an adjudicated finding of infringement. (plaintiffs' counsel report)

reputation.claim: Glassdoor showed Databricks at 4.0/5 from 1,712 reviews, with 77% recommending it to a friend, 92% CEO approval and 87% positive business outlook. (aggregator data)
On Glassdoor, the weakest listed category scores were work/life balance at 3.3/5 and senior management at 3.7/5; the page's six-month trend rose from roughly 3.8 to 4.2. (aggregator data)

red_flags.claim: The latest disclosed private valuation is $190 billion against a company-reported $7 billion revenue run-rate and >80% year-over-year growth; sustaining that growth and valuation is a key diligence sensitivity. (company-reported metrics; investment interpretation)

Databricks and MosaicML face an ongoing copyright litigation risk around training data and DBRX allegations; the opened court docket confirms the complaint, while plaintiffs' counsel reports the 2026 motion-to-dismiss development. (court record and plaintiffs' counsel report)

Revelio Labs reported employee growth alongside a 12% decline in active job postings in 2026, which warrants checking whether hiring pace is normalizing despite continued expansion. (aggregator estimate; investment interpretation)
Employee sentiment is positive overall but comparatively weaker on work/life balance and senior management, according to Glassdoor's aggregated scores. (aggregator data)

output.verdict: Databricks shows unusually strong enterprise traction, rapid company-reported growth, a broad founder/executive bench, and high-value customer and partnership evidence. The investment case needs a closer look at the $190 billion private valuation versus non-audited run-rate metrics, the durability and margin profile of AI-driven growth, the pace and quality of hiring, and the unresolved MosaicML/DBRX copyright litigation.
missing_fields: complete funding-round history and fully verified cumulative capital raised
audited financial statements and GAAP profitability
notable executive departures in the last 2 years
independent confirmation of customer counts, run-rate metrics and valuation
